summary: This bill authorizes appropriations for fiscal year 2026 for Department of Defense military activities, military construction, and Department of Energy defense activities, prescribes military personnel strengths for that year, and reforms procurement processes to streamline acquisition and enhance defense capabilities.

scores.thoughts: This bill is the National Defense Authorization Act for FY2026, authorizing over $152 billion in procurement, $142 billion in RDT&E, and $295 billion in O&M, among other categories. It significantly expands government spending on defense, with no provisions for reductions. The scale is -1 for expand, +1 for reduce, so this is a strong expansion.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxation, higher or lower taxes, or changes to tax policy.

The bill includes expansions to TRICARE coverage for fertility treatment, contraception, midwife services, and other health benefits, but these are minor compared to the overall bill. No shift to public/universal or private/market-based. Tangential at best.
No provisions on gun regulations or rights.
No direct bearing on immigration pathways or border enforcement.
No provisions related to abortion access or restrictions.

The bill is primarily the NDAA, authorizing massive increases in military procurement ($152B), RDT&E ($142B), O&M ($295B), personnel ($181B), and construction ($18B). It is fundamentally about increasing military and defense spending.
Some ERCIP projects for energy resilience, but minor compared to overall bill. No major environmental protections or deregulation.
No provisions on welfare, food stamps, etc.
Minor funding for JROTC, National Defense Education Program, but no public school investment or school choice.
Funding for drug interdiction and counter-drug activities ($904M), stricter enforcement. Minor but positive for stricter policy.
No provisions on sentencing or policing.
Some protectionist measures like Berry Amendment expansions, domestic sourcing preferences. Medium impact.
Massive spending authorizations with no debt reduction measures. Accepts deficit spending.
Prohibits gender transition services for minors in EFMP, limits legal protections. Strong restriction.
Authorizes Ukraine Security Assistance ($357M), Baltic Security Initiative, Taiwan, etc. Expands foreign aid.
No provisions.
Cybersecurity enhancements, AI strategies, but also expansions in tech procurement. Less regulation on tech in some areas, more oversight in others. Net 0.
No provisions.
No direct provisions.
